response: The continuity of care experience for residents in an academic vascular department is often limited, as they may not be able to follow patients throughout their entire treatment journey due to factors such as rotation schedules and service commitments. This can hinder their ability to learn complete surgical care, as they may not have the opportunity to see patients from initial consultation to post-operative follow-up. As a result, trainees may not gain a comprehensive understanding of the entire surgical process, including pre-operative planning, intra-operative decision-making, and post-operative management. To address this issue, vascular departments can implement strategies such as longitudinal clinics, mentorship programs, and electronic health record tracking to enhance residents' continuity of care experience and provide a more complete learning experience.
